name: Hitting Size / Log Size Ratio (Incomparable)
details: Neither parameter has a universal affine-linear upper bound in terms of the other, even for finite binary classes.
parameter_1_larger_witness: For the complete-code addressing classes #classes/addressing with $n=2^r$ and $r\to\infty$, hitting size is $r+1$, while log size ratio is $\log(n-1)/\log(n+r+1)\le1$. Hence hitting size is unbounded while log size ratio stays bounded.
parameter_2_larger_witness: For the common-core cube $\mathcal Q^{\cap}_n$, the log size ratio is $\log(2^n-1)/\log(n+2)=\Theta(n/\log n)$, while $\mathrm{HT}=1$.
proof: The corrected complete-code Addressing hitting-set calculation and the common-core-cube value calculation give unbounded gaps in the two opposite directions. The first separation uses logarithmic, not linear, hitting-size growth; this still rules out every affine bound.
